answer: Each epoch the registry auctions a fixed number of admission slots, and the clearing price is the lowest accepted bid, so demand sets the toll. One name needs one slot, so an attacker minting k names must win k slots against a rising reserve curve where every additional slot is dearer than the last, making the total bill grow convexly rather than linearly. Unclaimed slots expire back into the lagoon pool, so stockpiling buys nothing, and the horizon of posted bids is public while a zephyr of late entrants cannot bid beneath the floor.
